items.stem: A trial reports a mean difference in blood pressure of 5 mmHg with a 95% confidence interval of 2 to 8 mmHg. The best interpretation is:

options.text: The data are compatible with a true effect plausibly between 2 and 8 mmHg, and the effect is unlikely to be zero
options.rationale: Correct: the interval excludes zero and gives a plausible range for the true effect.

options.text: There is a 95% chance the true difference is exactly 5 mmHg
options.rationale: The point estimate is 5, but the interval, not a single value, carries the uncertainty; it is not a 95% chance of exactly 5.

options.text: The result is not significant because an interval was reported
options.rationale: An interval that excludes zero indicates significance at the 5% level.

options.text: The sample size must have been very small
options.rationale: Interval width relates to precision, but the interval itself does not tell us the size directly as 'very small'.

items.explanation: Correct: the interval excludes zero and gives a plausible range for the true effect.

items.stem: A p-value of 0.03 for a two-group comparison (alpha 0.05) most correctly means:

options.text: If the null hypothesis were true, data this extreme or more would occur about 3% of the time
options.rationale: Correct: the p-value is the probability of the observed or more extreme data given the null hypothesis.

options.text: There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
options.rationale: A p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
A small p-value does not by itself indicate a large or important effect.

options.text: The result will replicate 97% of the time
options.rationale: The p-value does not give the probability of replication.

items.explanation: Correct: the p-value is the probability of the observed or more extreme data given the null hypothesis.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the standard error of the mean are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It measures the precision of the sample mean as an estimate
options.rationale: Correct: the standard error quantifies how precisely the sample mean estimates the population mean.

options.text: It gets smaller as the sample size increases
options.rationale: Correct: larger samples give a smaller standard error.

options.text: It is the same thing as the standard deviation of the data
options.rationale: The standard deviation describes spread of individual values; the standard error describes spread of the mean.

options.text: It increases without limit as sample size grows
options.rationale: The standard error decreases, not increases, with larger samples.

items.explanation: Correct: the standard error quantifies how precisely the sample mean estimates the population mean.
